queries.title: Which heroes do developers touch the most?
queries.question: Per game, which heroes were changed most often, and are they mostly being buffed or nerfed?
queries.why: Frequent changes signal a hero the developers can't get right, a design problem rather than a numbers problem.
queries.sql:
SELECT
    game,
    hero,
    COUNT(*)                                          AS total_changes,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE change_type = 'buff')      AS buffs,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE change_type = 'nerf')      AS nerfs,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE change_type IN ('rework', 'adjustment')) AS reworks_or_adjustments,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE change_type = 'buff')
      - COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE change_type = 'nerf')  AS net_direction,   -- >0 = mostly buffed
    MIN(patch_date)                                   AS first_change,
    MAX(patch_date)                                   AS last_change
FROM patch_changes
WHERE change_type <> 'new'
GROUP BY game, hero
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY total_changes DESC, hero) <= 5
ORDER BY game, total_changes DESC;
queries.takeaway: Most-patched: deadlock: Shiv (18 changes, 10 nerfs / 5 buffs); marvel-rivals: Gambit (11 changes, 7 nerfs / 1 buffs); overwatch: Vendetta (15 changes, 6 nerfs / 6 buffs).

queries.title: Rolling 30-day win-rate leaders by role
queries.question: Right now, which heroes have the best match-weighted win rate over the last 30 days in each role? Covers every game with daily match counts.
queries.techniques: window aggregates with a RANGE frame (rolling sums), JOIN, two-stage QUALIFY (latest day per game, then top 3 per role)
queries.why: A rolling window smooths daily noise, and weighting by matches stops a low-volume day from swinging the number.
queries.sql:
WITH daily AS (
    SELECT d.game, d.date, d.hero, h.role, d.wins, d.matches
    FROM hero_daily d
    JOIN heroes h USING (game, hero)
    WHERE d.game IN (SELECT game FROM games WHERE stats_format = 'matches')   -- any game with real win/match counts
),
rolling AS (
    SELECT *,
        SUM(wins)    OVER w AS wins_30d,
        SUM(matches) OVER w AS matches_30d
    FROM daily
    WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY game, hero ORDER BY date
                 RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL 29 DAYS PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
),
latest AS (
    SELECT * FROM rolling
    QUALIFY date = MAX(date) OVER (PARTITION BY game)
)
SELECT
    game,
    role,
    hero,
    ROUND(100.0 * wins_30d / matches_30d, 2) AS win_rate_30d,
    matches_30d
FROM latest
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game, role ORDER BY wins_30d / matches_30d DESC) <= 3
ORDER BY game, role, win_rate_30d DESC;
queries.takeaway: Best 30-day win rate: deadlock: Graves (Mystic) at 57.3% over 2,930,033 games.

queries.title: Patch whiplash: buffed, then nerfed within a month
queries.question: How often does a hero get changed one way and then reversed within 30 days?
queries.techniques: LAG() over an ordered partition, date arithmetic, filtering on window results
queries.why: Quick reversals point to over-corrections, a balance process that's reacting instead of predicting.
queries.sql:
WITH ordered AS (
    SELECT
        game, hero, patch_date, change_type,
        LAG(change_type) OVER w AS previous_change,
        LAG(patch_date)  OVER w AS previous_date
    FROM patch_changes
    WHERE change_type IN ('buff', 'nerf')
    WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY game, hero ORDER BY patch_date)
)
SELECT
    game,
    hero,
    previous_date,
    previous_change,
    patch_date                    AS reversed_on,
    change_type                   AS reversed_with,
    patch_date - previous_date    AS days_between
FROM ordered
WHERE previous_change IS NOT NULL
  AND previous_change <> change_type
  AND patch_date - previous_date <= 30
ORDER BY reversed_on DESC, game, hero;   -- tie-breakers keep the output order stable between runs
queries.takeaway: 91 reversals within 30 days (deadlock: 59, marvel-rivals: 21, overwatch: 11); 21 were reversed within a week.

queries.title: Do big patches bring players back?
queries.question: For each big patch (10+ heroes changed), how did average Steam players in the week after compare with the week before?
queries.techniques: CTEs, range join on dates, conditional aggregation, percentage change
queries.why: Ties balance work to a business outcome, player engagement, which is the question a game studio actually cares about.
queries.sql:
WITH big AS (
    SELECT game, patch_date, title, heroes_changed
    FROM patches
    WHERE heroes_changed >= 10
),
windows AS (
    SELECT
        b.game, b.patch_date, b.title, b.heroes_changed,
        AVG(p.avg_players) FILTER (WHERE p.date BETWEEN b.patch_date - 7 AND b.patch_date - 1) AS players_before,
        AVG(p.avg_players) FILTER (WHERE p.date BETWEEN b.patch_date + 1 AND b.patch_date + 7) AS players_after,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.date < b.patch_date) AS days_before,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.date > b.patch_date) AS days_after
    FROM big b
    JOIN players_daily p
      ON p.game = b.game
     AND p.date BETWEEN b.patch_date - 7 AND b.patch_date + 7
    GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT
    game,
    patch_date,
    title,
    heroes_changed,
    ROUND(players_before)                                          AS players_before,
    ROUND(players_after)                                           AS players_after,
    ROUND(100.0 * (players_after - players_before) / players_before, 1) AS pct_change
FROM windows
WHERE days_before >= 5 AND days_after >= 5      -- skip periods where only monthly history exists
ORDER BY patch_date DESC;
rows: Reign of Talon Season 5: A Grim Doctrine
queries.takeaway: Players rose in the week after 61% of big patches (median change +2.1%). Biggest jump: marvel-rivals, Season 11: Doomsday balance update (+36.4%).

queries.title: Which days are busiest?
queries.question: Relative to its own weekly average, how many more (or fewer) players does each game have on each day of the week?
queries.techniques: date functions (dayname, isodow, date_trunc), window AVG per week for normalization, complete-week filter
queries.why: Normalizing by week removes growth and decline trends, leaving the pure weekly rhythm. That's useful for timing events and patches.
queries.sql:
WITH d AS (
    SELECT
        game, date, avg_players,
        AVG(avg_players) OVER (PARTITION BY game, date_trunc('week', date)) AS week_mean,
        COUNT(*)         OVER (PARTITION BY game, date_trunc('week', date)) AS days_in_week
    FROM players_daily
    WHERE date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM players_daily) - INTERVAL 120 DAYS
)
SELECT
    game,
    dayname(date)                                        AS weekday,
    isodow(date)                                         AS day_number,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(avg_players / week_mean - 1), 1)   AS pct_vs_week_average,
    COUNT(*)                                             AS weeks_used
FROM d
WHERE days_in_week = 7                                   -- complete weeks only
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY game, day_number;
queries.takeaway: deadlock: busiest Sunday (+13%), quietest Thursday (-7%); marvel-rivals: busiest Saturday (+11%), quietest Thursday (-10%); overwatch: busiest Sunday (+12%), quietest Thursday (-10%).

queries.title: Is the meta getting more or less diverse?
queries.question: Each month, how concentrated are hero picks? Measured as the effective number of heroes (1 / HHI), that number as a share of the roster, and the top-5 share of all picks. Covers every game with daily match counts.
queries.techniques: window SUM for shares, ROW_NUMBER ranking, sum of squares (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index), monthly roll-up per game
queries.why: HHI is the economist's market-concentration measure. Here it turns "is the game balanced?" into a number you can track. Dividing by the roster size controls for new heroes being added.
queries.sql:
WITH shares AS (
    SELECT
        game, date, hero,
        matches * 1.0 / SUM(matches) OVER (PARTITION BY game, date) AS pick_share
    FROM hero_daily
    WHERE game IN (SELECT game FROM games WHERE stats_format = 'matches')
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game, date ORDER BY pick_share DESC) AS rk
    FROM shares
),
per_day AS (
    SELECT
        game, date,
        SUM(pick_share * pick_share)              AS hhi,
        SUM(pick_share) FILTER (WHERE rk <= 5)    AS top5_share,
        COUNT(*)                                  AS heroes_played
    FROM ranked
    GROUP BY game, date
)
SELECT
    game,
    strftime(date_trunc('month', date), '%Y-%m')   AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(1 / hhi), 1)                         AS effective_heroes,
    MAX(heroes_played)                             AS heroes_available,
    ROUND(100 * AVG((1 / hhi) / heroes_played), 1) AS diversity_pct_of_roster,   -- 100% = every hero picked equally
    ROUND(100 * AVG(top5_share), 1)                AS top5_pick_share_pct
FROM per_day
GROUP BY game, month
ORDER BY game, month;
queries.takeaway: deadlock: effective heroes went from 28.2 (2025-10) to 38.8 (2026-11), while diversity relative to roster size moved from 88.1% to 88.3%, so the rise comes from new heroes being added, not from a more balanced meta.

queries.title: Do players ban the right heroes?
queries.question: In every game that publishes ban rates, how strongly does ban rate track win rate and pick rate? Which heroes are banned the most despite a below-average win rate?
queries.techniques: CORR(), arg_max, PERCENT_RANK window, latest-snapshot filter
queries.why: Bans are a player perception signal. Comparing them with results shows where perception and data disagree.
queries.sql:
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM hero_daily
    WHERE game IN (SELECT game FROM games WHERE has_ban_rates)   -- any game that publishes ban rates
      AND ban_rate IS NOT NULL
    QUALIFY date = MAX(date) OVER (PARTITION BY game)
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY ban_rate) AS ban_pctile,
        AVG(win_rate)  OVER (PARTITION BY game)                   AS game_avg_wr
    FROM latest
)
SELECT
    game,
    COUNT(*)                                         AS heroes,
    ROUND(CORR(ban_rate, win_rate), 2)               AS corr_ban_vs_win,
    ROUND(CORR(ban_rate, pick_rate), 2)              AS corr_ban_vs_pick,
    arg_max(hero, ban_rate)                          AS most_banned,
    ROUND(MAX(ban_rate), 1)                          AS top_ban_rate,
    string_agg(hero, ', ' ORDER BY ban_rate DESC)
        FILTER (WHERE ban_pctile >= 0.8 AND win_rate < game_avg_wr) AS overbanned_below_avg_wr
FROM ranked
GROUP BY game
ORDER BY game;
rows: Phoenix, Spider-Man, Gambit, Emma Frost, Elsa Bloodstone, Winter Soldier, Namor
Zarya, Jetpack Cat, Roadhog, Orisa, Mauga, Ana
queries.takeaway: marvel-rivals: ban vs. win-rate correlation +0.08, most banned Devil Dinosaur (38%). overwatch: ban vs. win-rate correlation -0.02, most banned Zarya (39%). Bans track perception more than results.

queries.title: Underused team-up loadouts
queries.question: For which heroes does the less popular team-up loadout have a higher win rate with its partner than the popular one? Covers every game with team-up data (currently Marvel Rivals).
queries.techniques: ROW_NUMBER, pivot with conditional MAX(CASE ...), derived comparison column
queries.why: A gap between popularity and performance is an "insight you can act on": a free win-rate edge most players are ignoring.
queries.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game, hero ORDER BY usage_share DESC) AS rk
    FROM teamups
    WHERE usage_share IS NOT NULL
),
pivoted AS (
    SELECT
        game,
        hero,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 1 THEN loadout END)          AS popular_loadout,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 1 THEN usage_share END)      AS popular_share,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 1 THEN wr_with_partner END)  AS popular_wr_with_partner,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 2 THEN loadout END)          AS other_loadout,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 2 THEN usage_share END)      AS other_share,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 2 THEN wr_with_partner END)  AS other_wr_with_partner
    FROM ranked
    GROUP BY game, hero
)
SELECT
    game,
    hero,
    popular_loadout,
    ROUND(popular_share, 1)                                        AS popular_share_pct,
    ROUND(popular_wr_with_partner, 1)                              AS popular_wr,
    other_loadout,
    ROUND(other_share, 1)                                          AS other_share_pct,
    ROUND(other_wr_with_partner, 1)                                AS other_wr,
    ROUND(other_wr_with_partner - popular_wr_with_partner, 1)      AS other_loadout_edge
FROM pivoted
WHERE other_wr_with_partner > popular_wr_with_partner
  AND hero NOT LIKE 'Deadpool (%'          -- Deadpool's three role variants share one set of loadouts
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY other_wr_with_partner - popular_wr_with_partner DESC) <= 12
ORDER BY game, other_loadout_edge DESC;
queries.takeaway: marvel-rivals: 12 heroes have an underused loadout that wins more often; biggest gap is Rocket Raccoon's Planet X Pals (37% usage), which wins +10.1 pts more than Mammalian Bond.

queries.title: Data quality check: do the matchup numbers agree with each other?
queries.question: If hero A wins X% against hero B, then B should win (100 - X)% against A, over the same number of games. Does the matchup data pass that test?
queries.techniques: self-join, symmetric pair de-duplication (a.hero < a.enemy), validation metrics
queries.why: Checking a source against its own logic before trusting it is basic data-quality practice, and an easy way to catch a broken feed.
queries.sql:
SELECT
    a.game,
    COUNT(*)                                                       AS hero_pairs_checked,
    ROUND(AVG(ABS(a.win_rate + b.win_rate - 100)), 3)              AS avg_deviation_pts,
    ROUND(MAX(ABS(a.win_rate + b.win_rate - 100)), 3)              AS max_deviation_pts,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.matches = b.matches)                  AS pairs_with_equal_game_counts,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ABS(a.win_rate + b.win_rate - 100) > 0.5) AS pairs_failing_0_5pt_tolerance
FROM matchups a
JOIN matchups b
  ON a.game = b.game
 AND a.hero = b.enemy
 AND a.enemy = b.hero
WHERE a.hero < a.enemy
GROUP BY a.game
ORDER BY a.game;
queries.takeaway: deadlock: PASS, 946 matchup pairs, average deviation 0.013 pts, max 0.04 pts, 0 outside a 0.5-pt tolerance.

queries.title: This week's biggest movers, and whether a patch explains them
queries.question: Which heroes' win rates changed most between the last 7 days and the 7 days before? Was each mover patched in that period? Covers every game with daily match counts.
queries.techniques: per-game date bounds, conditional aggregation, ROW_NUMBER partitioned by game, LEFT JOIN with string_agg
queries.why: Separating "moved because of a patch" from "moved on its own" is the first question to ask about any metric change.
queries.sql:
WITH match_games AS (
    SELECT game FROM games WHERE stats_format = 'matches'
),
bounds AS (
    SELECT game, MAX(date) AS last_day
    FROM hero_daily
    WHERE game IN (SELECT game FROM match_games)
    GROUP BY game
),
weekly AS (
    SELECT
        d.game,
        d.hero,
        SUM(d.wins)    FILTER (WHERE d.date >  b.last_day - 7)                              AS wins_now,
        SUM(d.matches) FILTER (WHERE d.date >  b.last_day - 7)                              AS games_now,
        SUM(d.wins)    FILTER (WHERE d.date <= b.last_day - 7 AND d.date > b.last_day - 14) AS wins_prev,
        SUM(d.matches) FILTER (WHERE d.date <= b.last_day - 7 AND d.date > b.last_day - 14) AS games_prev
    FROM hero_daily d
    JOIN bounds b USING (game)
    GROUP BY d.game, d.hero
),
moves AS (
    SELECT
        game, hero,
        100.0 * wins_now / games_now   AS wr_now,
        100.0 * wins_prev / games_prev AS wr_prev,
        100.0 * wins_now / games_now - 100.0 * wins_prev / games_prev AS change_pts,
        games_now
    FROM weekly
    WHERE games_now >= 5000 AND games_prev >= 5000
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY change_pts DESC) AS up_rank,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY change_pts ASC)  AS down_rank
    FROM moves
),
patched AS (
    SELECT c.game, c.hero,
        string_agg(c.change_type || ' (' || strftime(c.patch_date, '%b %d') || ')', ', ') AS recent_patch
    FROM patch_changes c
    JOIN bounds b USING (game)
    WHERE c.patch_date > b.last_day - 14
    GROUP BY c.game, c.hero
)
SELECT
    r.game,
    CASE WHEN up_rank <= 5 THEN 'riser' ELSE 'faller' END AS direction,
    r.hero,
    ROUND(wr_prev, 2)    AS win_rate_prev_week,
    ROUND(wr_now, 2)     AS win_rate_this_week,
    ROUND(change_pts, 2) AS change_pts,
    games_now            AS games_this_week,
    COALESCE(p.recent_patch, 'no patch: moved on its own') AS explained_by
FROM ranked r
LEFT JOIN patched p USING (game, hero)
WHERE up_rank <= 5 OR down_rank <= 5
ORDER BY r.game, change_pts DESC;

queries.title: Did Marvel Rivals take Overwatch's players, and did Deadlock take players from both?
queries.question: Using monthly average Steam players: was Overwatch's drop after Marvel Rivals launched (Dec 2024) unusual for Overwatch? Do the games' monthly changes move against each other? When Deadlock surged, did the other two lose players?
queries.techniques: monthly roll-up + pivot, rolling 3-month averages, event study ranked against the game's own history (PERCENT_RANK placebo), CORR() with a noise threshold, LAG-based % changes, UNION ALL of tests
queries.why: "Game A took game B's players" is a causal claim, and aggregate counts can't show individuals switching. The defensible test is whether one game's losses line up with another's gains more than that game's normal swings would explain. Caveats: Steam only (most Overwatch players are on Battle.net and consoles); before 2026 the source kept about one figure per month, which is noisy.
queries.sql:
WITH monthly AS (                       -- one average per game per month, complete months only
    SELECT game, date_trunc('month', date) AS month, AVG(avg_players) AS players
    FROM players_daily
    WHERE date < date_trunc('month', (SELECT MAX(date) FROM players_daily))
    GROUP BY game, month
),
wide AS (
    SELECT month,
        MAX(players) FILTER (WHERE game = 'overwatch')     AS ow,
        MAX(players) FILTER (WHERE game = 'marvel-rivals') AS mr,
        MAX(players) FILTER (WHERE game = 'deadlock')      AS dl
    FROM monthly
    GROUP BY month
),
changes AS (                            -- month-over-month % change per game
    SELECT month,
        100.0 * (ow / LAG(ow) OVER (ORDER BY month) - 1) AS ow_chg,
        100.0 * (mr / LAG(mr) OVER (ORDER BY month) - 1) AS mr_chg,
        100.0 * (dl / LAG(dl) OVER (ORDER BY month) - 1) AS dl_chg
    FROM wide
),

-- Test 1: Overwatch around Marvel Rivals' launch, ranked against every other period in Overwatch's history.
ow_roll AS (
    SELECT month, AVG(ow) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS ow_3mo
    FROM wide WHERE ow IS NOT NULL
),
ow_windows AS (
    SELECT month,
        100.0 * (ow_3mo / LAG(ow_3mo, 3) OVER (ORDER BY month) - 1) AS chg_next_3mo,   -- this 3 months vs the 3 before
        100.0 * (ow_3mo / LAG(ow_3mo, 6) OVER (ORDER BY month) - 1) AS chg_months_4_6  -- months 4-6 vs the 3 before the gap
    FROM ow_roll
),
ow_ranked AS (
    SELECT month, chg_next_3mo, chg_months_4_6,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY chg_next_3mo)   AS pctile_3mo,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY chg_months_4_6) AS pctile_4_6,
        COUNT(chg_next_3mo) OVER ()                   AS windows
    FROM ow_windows
    WHERE month >= '2024-02-01'                 -- skip Overwatch's own Steam-launch hype (Aug-Oct 2023)
      AND chg_next_3mo IS NOT NULL
),
launch AS (
    SELECT
        MAX(chg_next_3mo) FILTER (WHERE month = '2025-02-01')   AS drop_3mo,      -- Dec-Feb vs Sep-Nov
        MAX(pctile_3mo)   FILTER (WHERE month = '2025-02-01')   AS pct_3mo,
        MAX(chg_months_4_6) FILTER (WHERE month = '2025-05-01') AS drop_4_6,      -- Mar-May vs Sep-Nov
        MAX(pctile_4_6)   FILTER (WHERE month = '2025-05-01')   AS pct_4_6,
        MAX(windows)                                            AS windows
    FROM ow_ranked
),

-- Test 2: do monthly changes move together (shared drivers) or against each other (substitution)?
pairs AS (
    SELECT 'Overwatch vs. Marvel Rivals' AS games, CORR(ow_chg, mr_chg) AS r, COUNT(ow_chg + mr_chg) AS n FROM changes
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Overwatch vs. Deadlock',     CORR(ow_chg, dl_chg), COUNT(ow_chg + dl_chg) FROM changes
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Marvel Rivals vs. Deadlock', CORR(mr_chg, dl_chg), COUNT(mr_chg + dl_chg) FROM changes
),

-- Test 3: Deadlock's three biggest surges since Marvel Rivals launched, and how the other two did in those months,
-- ranked against their own monthly changes (0% = worst month, 100% = best month).
ranked_changes AS (
    SELECT month, dl_chg, ow_chg, mr_chg,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ow_chg) AS ow_pctile,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY mr_chg) AS mr_pctile,
        COUNT(*) OVER ()                      AS months
    FROM changes
    WHERE ow_chg IS NOT NULL AND mr_chg IS NOT NULL AND dl_chg IS NOT NULL
),
surges AS (
    SELECT * FROM ranked_changes
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY dl_chg DESC) <= 3
)

SELECT '1. Marvel Rivals launch' AS test,
       'Overwatch: Dec 2024-Feb 2025 vs. the 3 months before' AS measure,
       ROUND(drop_3mo, 1) AS change_pct,
       ROUND(100 * pct_3mo) AS pctile_in_own_history,          -- low = an unusually bad stretch for that game
       windows AS compared_with,
       CASE WHEN pct_3mo <= 0.05 THEN 'One of Overwatch''s worst stretches ever: strong sign Marvel Rivals pulled players'
            WHEN pct_3mo <= 0.20 THEN 'Worse than most stretches but not exceptional: suggestive, not conclusive'
            ELSE 'A normal swing for Overwatch' END AS reading
FROM launch
UNION ALL
SELECT '1. Marvel Rivals launch', 'Overwatch: Mar-May 2025 vs. before launch (did it recover?)',
       ROUND(drop_4_6, 1), ROUND(100 * pct_4_6), windows,
       CASE WHEN drop_4_6 > -5 THEN 'Recovered to its pre-launch level'
            WHEN pct_4_6 <= 0.20 THEN 'Still well below pre-launch: a lasting loss'
            ELSE 'Somewhat below pre-launch, within normal variation' END
FROM launch
UNION ALL
SELECT '2. Co-movement', games || ': correlation of monthly % changes',
       ROUND(r, 2), NULL, n,
       CASE WHEN ABS(r) < 2 / SQRT(n) THEN 'No reliable relationship (|r| under the ~2/sqrt(n) noise threshold)'
            WHEN r < 0 THEN 'Move in opposite directions: consistent with players moving between them'
            ELSE 'Move together: shared drivers (holidays, summer, genre interest), not substitution' END
FROM pairs
UNION ALL
SELECT '3. Deadlock surges', 'Overwatch in ' || strftime(month, '%b %Y') || ' (Deadlock ' || printf('%+.0f', dl_chg) || '%)',
       ROUND(ow_chg, 1), ROUND(100 * ow_pctile), months,
       CASE WHEN ow_pctile <= 0.20 THEN 'One of Overwatch''s weaker months: consistent with losing players to Deadlock'
            WHEN ow_pctile >= 0.80 THEN 'One of Overwatch''s better months: no sign of losing players'
            ELSE 'An ordinary month for Overwatch' END
FROM surges
UNION ALL
SELECT '3. Deadlock surges', 'Marvel Rivals in ' || strftime(month, '%b %Y') || ' (Deadlock ' || printf('%+.0f', dl_chg) || '%)',
       ROUND(mr_chg, 1), ROUND(100 * mr_pctile), months,
       CASE WHEN mr_pctile <= 0.20 THEN 'One of Marvel Rivals'' weaker months: consistent with losing players to Deadlock'
            WHEN mr_pctile >= 0.80 THEN 'One of Marvel Rivals'' better months: no sign of losing players'
            ELSE 'An ordinary month for Marvel Rivals' END
FROM surges
ORDER BY test, measure;

Suggestive of a pull, not proof; during Deadlock's 3 biggest surges, Overwatch fell in 1 and had an unusually weak month in 0; during Deadlock's 3 biggest surges, Marvel Rivals fell in 3 and had an unusually weak month in 1; no pair of games' monthly changes correlates beyond noise.
